titleEn: The Glory of Kings — Menelik's Blessing and the Mourning of Jerusalem (ch. 49–50)
part: ch. 49–50 — Menelik's Blessing and the Mourning of Jerusalem
about: Menelik takes his father's blessing and sets out for Ethiopia; Zion is secretly loaded onto a cart, the city discovers its loss in grief, and Solomon, weeping, recalls the prophecies that law and wisdom would pass to other peoples.

sentences.t: ፵፱ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ባረኮ ፡ አቡሁ ፡ ለወልዱ ።
sentences.l: 49. Where blessed-him his-father to-his-son
sentences.i: Chapter 49: Where his father blessed his son
sentences.n: Chapter heading. ኀበ here 'where / at the point where', followed by a past verb (ባረኮ 'he blessed him'); ለወልዱ 'to/for his son' — ለ- marks the person blessed. Geʿez numerals ፵፱ = 49.

sentences.t: ወእምዝ ፡ ተንሥአ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይሖር ፡ ብሔሮ ፡ ወቦአ ፡ ኀበ ፡ አቡሁ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይጸሊ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ወይቤሎ ፡ ባርከኒ ፡ አባ ፡ ወሰገደ ፡ ሎቱ ።
sentences.l: And-after-this arose king-of Ethiopia that-he-might-go (to) his-country, and-entered to his-father that-he-might-pray for-him, and-said-to-him, 'bless-me, father', and-bowed to-him.
sentences.i: After this the king of Ethiopia rose to go to his own country. He went in to his father to pray for him (?), and said to him, 'Bless me, father,' and bowed before him.
sentences.n: ተንሥአ 'arose' (perfect 3rd masc. sing.); ንጉሠ is the construct form of ንጉሥ 'king' — 'king-of Ethiopia' — so the king is Menelik, here Ethiopia's king. ከመ ይሖር 'that he might go' (ከመ + subjunctive ይሖር). ወቦአ 'and he entered'; ኀበ 'to'. ይጸሊ ሎቱ — ጸለየ 'pray'; with ሎቱ ('to/for him') the sense may be 'pray for him' or 'pray with/before him' (?). ወይቤሎ = ወ + ይቤ 'he said' + ሎ 'to him'; ባርከኒ imperative + 'me'.

sentences.t: ወአንሥኦ ፡ ወባረኮ ፡ ወአኀዞ ፡ ርእሶ ፡ ወይቤ ፤
sentences.l: And-he-raised-him and-blessed-him and-took-hold-of-him (by) his-head, and-said:
sentences.i: His father raised him up, blessed him, and took hold of his head (?), and said:
sentences.n: Each verb carries 'him' as the suffix -ኦ, fused with the verb's last vowel (አንሥኦ, ባረኮ, አኀዞ). አኀዞ ርእሶ 'he took hold of him, his head' — 'took him by the head' or 'embraced his head' (?); ርእስ 'head' is also the Geʿez word for 'self', so a reflexive sense is possible. The subject of all three verbs is the father, who raises Menelik after he bows. ፤ ends the unit before the blessing begins.

sentences.t: ቡሩክ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ አምላኪየ ፡ ዘባረኮ ፡ ለአቡየ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ ወዘባረኮ ፡ ለአቡነ ፡ አብርሃም ፡ የሀሉ ፡ ምስሌከ ፡ በኵሉ ፡ ጊዜ ፡ ወይባርክ ፡ ዘርእከ ፡ በከመ ፡ ባረኮ ፡ ለያዕቆብ ፡ ወአብዝኀ ፡ ዘርኦ ፡ ከመ ፡ ኮከበ ፡ ሰማይ ፡ ወከመ ፡ ኆጻ ፡ ባሕር ፤
sentences.l: Blessed (is) God my-God, who-blessed-him to-my-father David and-who-blessed-him to-our-father Abraham: may-he-be with-you at-all time, and-may-he-bless your-seed, as he-blessed to-Jacob, and-multiplied his-seed like stars-of heaven and-like sand-of sea;
sentences.i: Blessed is God, my God, who blessed my father David and who blessed our father Abraham. May he be with you at all times and bless your seed, as he blessed Jacob and multiplied his seed like the stars of heaven and the sand of the sea;
sentences.n: ዘባረኮ ለአቡየ 'who blessed my father' — the relative ዘ- plus a verb with a pronoun 'him' that repeats the object (ለ- marks the object). የሀሉ and ይባርክ are jussives ('may he be', 'may he bless'). ዘርእከ 'your seed' (ዘርእ + ከ). Allusions: Genesis 22:17 (seed like the stars and the sand) and the blessing of Jacob (Genesis 28). The speaker is Solomon, so 'my father David'.

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ ባረኮ ፡ አብርሃም ፡ ለይስሐቅ ፡ አቡየ ፡ ከማሁ ፡ ይኩን ፡ በረከትከ ፡ እምጠለ ፡ ሰማይ ፡ ወእምስፍሓ ፡ ለምድር ፡ ወይትአዘዝ ፡ ለከ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ እንስሳ ፡ ወአዕዋፈ ፡ ሰማይ ፡ ወአራዊተ ፡ ገዳም ፡ ወዓሣተ ፡ ባሕር ፤
sentences.l: And-as blessed-him Abraham to-Isaac my-father, so may-be your-blessing from-dew-of heaven and-from-breadth-of-it (?) of-earth, and-be-subject to-you all livestock and-birds-of heaven and-beasts-of wilderness and-fish-of sea;
sentences.i: And as Abraham blessed my father Isaac, so may your blessing be from the dew of heaven and from the breadth of the earth (?), and may all livestock, the birds of heaven, the beasts of the wilderness, and the fish of the sea be subject to you;
sentences.n: በከመ … ከማሁ 'as … so'. The nouns in chains are construct: ጠለ ሰማይ 'dew-of heaven' (cf. Genesis 27:28, Isaac's blessing of Jacob). እምስፍሓ ለምድር 'from the breadth of the earth' — ስፍሕ 'width', with a pronoun -ሓ anticipating ለምድር; 'breadth' is my reading, where Genesis 27:28 has 'fatness' (?). ይትአዘዝ ለከ 'may it obey/be subject to you' (ተ-stem of አዘዘ 'command'), with ኵሉ እንስሳ 'all livestock' as the subject. The three nouns አዕዋፈ, አራዊተ, ዓሣተ are in the accusative, so they might instead be objects of an unstated verb; I read them as further subjects (?).

sentences.t: ኩን ፡ ምሉአ ፡ ወአኮ ፡ ንቱገ ፡ ኩን ፡ ፍጹመ ፡ ወአኮ ፡ ሕጹጸ ፡ ኩን ፡ የዋሀ ፡ ወአኮ ፡ ነቢረ ፡ ኩን ፡ ጥዑየ ፡ ወአኮ ፡ ሕሙመ ፡ ኩን ፡ ኄረ ፡ ወአኮ ፡ መስተቀይመ ፡ ኩን ፡ ንጹሐ ፡ ወአኮ ፡ ርሱሐ ፡ ኩን ፡ ጻድቀ ፡ ወአኮ ፡ ኃጥአ ፡ ኩን ፡ መሓሬ ፡ ወአኮ ፡ ዐማፄ ፡ ኩን ፡ ብሩሀ ፡ ወአኮ ፡ ፀዋገ ፡ ኩን ፡ መስተዐግሰ ፡ ወአኮ ፡ ምዑዐ ፤
sentences.l: Be full and-not ንቱግ (?); be perfect and-not deficient; be gentle and-not dweller (?) (ነቢር); be healthy and-not sick; be good and-not one-who-opposes (?) (መስተቀይም); be pure and-not filthy; be righteous and-not sinner; be merciful and-not wrongdoer; be bright and-not captor (?) (ፀዋግ); be patient and-not wrathful (?) (ምዑዕ);
sentences.i: Be full, and not wanting (?); be perfect, and not deficient; be gentle, and not a dweller (?); be healthy, and not sick; be good, and not one who opposes (?); be pure, and not filthy; be righteous, and not a sinner; be merciful, and not unjust; be bright, and not a captor (?); be patient, and not wrathful (?);
sentences.n: A run of paired commands: ኩን 'be!' (imperative of ኮነ) + an adjective in the accusative (ምሉአ, ፍጹመ …), then ወአኮ 'and not' + its opposite. Clear pairs: ፍጹም/ሕጹጽ 'perfect/deficient', ጥዑይ/ሕሙም 'healthy/sick', ንጹሕ/ርሱሕ 'pure/filthy', ጻድቅ/ኃጥእ 'righteous/sinner', መሓሪ/ዐማፂ 'merciful/wrongdoer'. Uncertain opposites: ንቱግ, ነቢር, መስተቀይም, ፀዋግ, ምዑዕ — the glosses given are guesses from the roots and are marked (?). ነቢረ may come from ነበረ 'sit, dwell' (the sense as the opposite of 'gentle' is unclear), and ምዑዕ I connect, as a guess, with a root for anger or heat (?).

sentences.t: ወይፍርሁከ ፡ ፀር ፡ ወይግረሩ ፡ ለከ ፡ ጸላእትከ ፡ ታሕተ ፡ መከይደ ፡ እገሪከ ፤
sentences.l: And-may-fear-you enemy, and-may-bow-down (?) to-you your-foes, beneath trampling-of your-feet;
sentences.i: May enemies fear you, and may your foes bow down to you (?) beneath the tread of your feet;
sentences.n: ወይፍርሁከ 'may they fear you' — jussive plural + 'you'; ፀር 'enemy' is collective. ይግረሩ ለከ — 'they will bow/grovel to you' is my guess (?). መከይደ 'trampling' is construct before እገሪከ 'of your feet'; compare Psalm 110:1 (footstool).

sentences.t: ወትኩን ፡ ለከ ፡ መርሐ ፡ እግዝእትየ ፡ ጽዮን ፡ ቅድስት ፡ ሰማያዊት ፡ ታቦተ ፡ ሕጉ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ በኵሉ ፡ ጊዜ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ኀለይከ ፡ በልብከ ፡ ወአንጸርከ ፡ በአጻብዒከ ፡ ዘርሑቅ ፡ ወዘቅሩብ ፡ ለከ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ዘትሑት ፡ ወዘልዑልለከ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ዘጽኑዕ ፡ ወዘድኩም ፡ ለከ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ዘአፍአ ፡ ወዘውስጥ ፡ ለከ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ዘቤት ፡ ወዘገዳም ፡ ለከ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ዘያስተርኢ ፡ ወዘኢያስተርኢ ፡ ለከ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ዘእቱት ፡ ወልጹቅ ፡ ለከ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ዘኅቡእ ፡ ወክሡት ፡ ለከ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ዘክቡት ፡ ወግሁድ ፡ ለከ ፡ ትኩንከ ፡ መርሐ ፡ እግዝእትነ ፡ ጽዮን ፡ ቅድስት ፡ ሰማያዊት ፡ ታቦተ ፡ ሕጉ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ንጽሕት ።
sentences.l: And-may-she-be for-you guide my-lady Zion, holy, heavenly, ark-of the-law of-God, at-all time, to-where you-have-thought in-your-heart and-looked-toward (?) with-your-fingers: that-which-far and-that-which-near for-you; to-where that-which-low and-that-which-high for-you; to-where that-which-strong and-that-which-weak for-you; to-where that-which-outside and-that-which-within for-you; to-where that-which-house and-that-which-wilderness for-you; to-where that-which-appears and-that-which-does-not-appear for-you; to-where that-which-እቱት (?) and-clinging for-you; to-where that-which-hidden and-revealed for-you; to-where that-which-closed and-manifest for-you — may-she-be-for-you guide, our-lady Zion, holy, heavenly, ark-of the-law of-God, pure.
sentences.i: May Zion, my lady — holy, heavenly, the Ark of the Law of God — be a guide to you at all times, wherever you have thought in your heart and pointed (?) with your fingers: whether far or near to you; wherever low or high; wherever strong or weak; outside or within; house or wilderness; visible or unseen; loose (?) or clinging; hidden or revealed; closed or open to view. May she be your guide, our lady Zion, holy, heavenly, the Ark of the Law of God, the pure one.
sentences.n: One long sentence with no ፤ to cut at, kept whole. The frame: ወትኩን ለከ መርሐ 'may she be a guide for you' (መርሐ accusative predicate), then ኀበ 'to where' + a pair of ዘ- phrases ('that which is …') repeated: nine pairs in all, the first (ዘርሑቅ ወዘቅሩብ) without a second ኀበ, the other eight each introduced by ኀበ, and every pair closing with ለከ 'for you'. Note ወዘልዑልለከ is written as one word (ወዘልዑል + ለከ). ዘእቱት is unclear (?); 'loose' is a guess from the contrast with 'clinging'. አንጸረ I know as 'look toward, regard'; 'pointed' is my reading of 'with your fingers' (?). The sentence then repeats the opening formula, ending with the adjective ንጽሕት 'pure' (feminine, agreeing with ጽዮን). ታቦተ ሕጉ ለእግዚኣብሔር 'ark-of the-law of-God': Zion is identified with the Ark, the book's central idea.

sentences.t: ወተባረከ ፡ ወሰገደ ፡ ወሖረ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: And-he-was-blessed and-bowed and-went. [chapter-end marks]
sentences.i: He was blessed, bowed, and went.
sentences.n: ተባረከ 'was blessed' (ተ-stem, passive/reflexive of ባረከ) — he received the blessing. The string of ፨ at the end is Bezold's chapter-end ornament, kept in the source.

sentences.t: ፶ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ተፋነዉ ፡ ምስለ ፡ አቡሁ ፡ ወላሐወት ፡ ሀገር ።
sentences.l: 50. Where they-parted with his-father, and-lamented city
sentences.i: Chapter 50: Where they took leave of one another with his father, and the city lamented
sentences.n: Chapter heading. ተፋነዉ 'they parted from one another / took leave' (ተ-stem of ፈነወ 'send' — reciprocal, so 'sent each other off'); ወላሐወት ሀገር 'and the city lamented' — ላሐወ I read as 'wail' (?); the verb is feminine because ሀገር 'city' is. ምስለ 'with'.

sentences.t: ወተፋነዉ ፡ ወሖሩ ፤
sentences.l: And-they-parted and-went;
sentences.i: They took leave of one another and went.
sentences.n: ወተፋነዉ 'and they parted' — perfect plural, as in the heading — then ወሖሩ 'and they went' (ሖሩ, perfect plural of ሖረ). The Ethiopians leave Jerusalem; ፤ marks the pause before the secret loading of the Ark.

sentences.t: ወአቅደሙ ፡ ጽዒኖታ ፡ ለጽዮን ፡ በሌሊት ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሰረገላ ፡ በኅሱራት ፡ ንዋያት ፡ ወርሱሓት ፡ አልባስ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ንዋይ ፡ ቊስቋሳት ፡ ወተጽዕኑ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ ሰረገላት ።
sentences.l: And-they-did-beforehand her-loading, of-Zion, by-night onto cart, with-poor (?) goods and-filthy garments, with goods ቊስቋሳት (?); and-were-loaded all carts.
sentences.i: They first loaded Zion by night onto a cart, among poor goods and filthy garments, together with ቊስቋሳት (?) wares; and all the carts were loaded.
sentences.n: አቅደሙ 'they did first / in advance' (አ-stem of ቀደመ 'precede'); ጽዒኖታ ለጽዮን 'her loading, Zion's' — ጽዒኖታ is ጽዒኖት 'loading' + -ሃ 'her' (ት+ሃ → ታ), anticipating ለጽዮን. The Ark is carried off in secret, hidden among ordinary baggage. ኅሱራት 'poor, deficient' and ርሱሓት 'filthy' are plural adjectives, placed before the nouns they describe ('poor ones of goods'), agreeing with ንዋያት 'goods' and አልባስ 'garments'; ቊስቋሳት is unclear (?). Taking these as a disguise is my reading from the context; it is not in the translation. ተጽዕኑ 'were loaded' (passive of ጽዕነ).

sentences.t: ወተንሡ ፡ ሊቃናት ፡ ወተነፍሐ ፡ ቀርን ፡ ወደምፀት ፡ ሀገር ፡ ወወውዑ ፡ መሐዛት ፡ ወከለላ ፡ ግርማ ፡ ወዖዳ ፡ ጸጋ ፤
sentences.l: And-rose chiefs, and-was-blown horn, and-the-city sounded (?), and-the መሐዛት (?) burned, and-covered-her (?) majesty, and-encircled-her (?) grace;
sentences.i: The chiefs rose, a horn was blown, and the city was in uproar (?); the መሐዛት (?) burned, majesty covered her (?) and grace encircled her (?);
sentences.n: ሊቃናት plural of ሊቅ 'chief, elder'. ተነፍሐ ቀርን 'a horn was blown' (passive; ቀርን 'horn'). The last four clauses are poetic and obscure: ደምፀት ሀገር (ደምፀ 'sound, cry'), ወወውዑ መሐዛት, ከለላ ግርማ ('majesty covered her' — ከለለ + -ሃ, the city; ግርማ 'majesty, awe'), ዖዳ ጸጋ ('grace encircled her' — ዖደ + -ሃ). Treat all four glosses as provisional (?).

sentences.t: አውየዉ ፡ ርሡኣን ፡ ወከልሑ ፡ ሕፃናት ፡ ወበከያ ፡ አቤራት ፡ ወላሐዋ ፡ ደናግል ፡ በእንተ ፡ ዘተንሥኡ ፡ ደቂቀ ፡ መኳንን ፡ ቲሆሙ ፡ ለኀያላነ ፡ እስራኤል ።
sentences.l: Cried-out old-men, and-shouted children, and-wept wives (?), and-lamented virgins, because-of those-who rose, sons-of nobles, ቲሆሙ (?) of-the-mighty-ones-of Israel.
sentences.i: The old men cried out, the children shouted, the wives wept (?), and the maidens lamented, for those who had risen up, the sons of the nobles, ቲሆሙ (?) of the mighty men of Israel.
sentences.n: Four verbs in the perfect with their subjects after them: አውየዉ ርሡኣን (ርሡእ 'aged', plural), ከልሑ ሕፃናት, በከያ አቤራት (አቤር = 'wives/widows' (?)), ላሐዋ ደናግል (ደናግል 'virgins'). በእንተ ዘተንሥኡ 'because of those who rose' — Menelik's companions, the firstborn sons of Israel's nobles. ቲሆሙ is unclear (?). ደቂቀ is the construct plural of ደቂቅ 'sons'. ለኀያላነ 'of the mighty': ኀያላነ is the construct plural of ኀያል; the ለ- before it I read as 'of' (?).

sentences.t: ወአኮ ፡ ባሕቲቶሙ ፡ በእንቲአሆሙ ፡ ዘትበኪ ፡ ሀገር ፡ አላ ፡ እስመ ፡ ተሀይደ ፡ ግርማሃ ፡ ለሀገር ፡ ምስሌሆሙ ፤
sentences.l: And-not by-themselves-alone on-account-of-them that-weeps the-city, but because was-taken-away (?) majesty-of-her, of-the-city, with-them;
sentences.i: And it was not for their sake alone that the city wept, but because the city's majesty had been taken away with them (?);
sentences.n: ወአኮ … አላ 'not … but'. ባሕቲቶሙ 'they alone'; ዘትበኪ is ዘ- + 3fs imperfect, 'for which she weeps'; በእንቲአሆሙ 'on their account'. ተሀይደ — a ተ-stem of ሀየደ; 'was taken away / departed' is my reading (?). ግርማሃ ለሀገር 'the city's majesty' — the possessive suffix -ሃ is anticipatory before ለሀገር.

sentences.t: ወሶበኒ ፡ ኢያእመሩ ፡ ገሃደ ፡ ከመ ፡ ተነሥአት ፡ ጽዮን ፡ እምኔሆሙ ፡ በልቦሙሰ ፡ ኢስሕቱ ፡ ወይበክዩ ፡ መሪረ ፡ ከመ ፡ አመ ፡ ቀተለ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ በኵሮሙ ፡ ለግብጽ ፡ ከማሁ ፡ ኮኑ ፡ ወአልቦ ፡ ቤተ ፡ ኀበ ፡ አልቦ ፡ አውያተ ፡ እምሰብእ ፡ እስከ ፡ እንስሳ ፡ ከለባትኒ ፡ የአውይዉ ፡ ወአእዱግኒ ፡ ይንህቁ ፡ ወኵሎሙ ፡ ኅቡረ ፡ ያውሕዙ ፡ አንብዖሙ ፡ እለ ፡ ተረፉ ፡ ህየ ፤
sentences.l: And-although not-they-knew openly that had-risen Zion from-among-them, in-their-hearts indeed not they-erred; and-they-wept bitterly, as when killed God the-firstborn-of-them of-Egypt, so they-were: and-there-was-not a-house where there-was-not wailing from men to livestock — dogs even howled, and-donkeys even brayed — and-all of-them together shed their-tears, those-who remained there;
sentences.i: Even though they did not know openly that Zion had risen up from among them, in their hearts they were not mistaken. They wept bitterly, as when God killed the firstborn of Egypt, so it was: there was no house without wailing, from people to livestock. Even the dogs howled and the donkeys brayed, and all together, those who remained there, let their tears flow;
sentences.n: ወሶበኒ 'and even when / although'; ገሃደ 'openly'; -ሰ in በልቦሙሰ is an emphatic enclitic ('in their hearts, indeed'). Allusion: the death of Egypt's firstborn and the cry that followed, Exodus 12:29–30. ወአልቦ ቤተ ኀበ አልቦ አውያተ 'there was no house where there was no wailing' (አልቦ 'there is not'). The -ኒ on ከለባትኒ and አእዱግኒ is 'even/also'. የአውይዉ and ይንህቁ are imperfects used for a vivid past. ያውሕዙ አንብዖሙ 'made their tears flow' (አ-stem).

sentences.t: ከመ ፡ ዘዐገትዋ ፡ መላእክተ ፡ ፀር ፡ ጽኑዓን ፡ ለዐባይ ፡ ሀገር ፡ ወሮድዋ ፡ ወማህረክዋ ፡ ወፄወውዋ ፡ ወቀተልዋ ፡ በአፈ ፡ ኀጺን ፡ ከማሁ ፡ ኮነት ፡ ሀገር ፡ ጽዮን ፡ ይእቲ ፡ እየሩሳሌም ፨
sentences.l: As that-which besieged-it messengers-of enemy, mighty, the-great city (ለ-), and-attacked-it (?) and-plundered-it (?) and-took-it-captive and-killed-it by-mouth-of iron — so was the-city Zion, that-is Jerusalem.
sentences.i: As when an enemy's mighty emissaries (?) besiege a great city, attack it (?), plunder it (?), take it captive, and put it to the sword, so it was with the city of Zion, that is Jerusalem.
sentences.n: ከመ ዘ 'as when / like that which' … ከማሁ ኮነት 'so it was': the simile of a sacked city. መላእክተ ፀር 'messengers-of enemy' — literally 'the enemy's messengers' (the same word as 'angels'), here probably envoys or troops (?). The verbs are plural perfects with 'it' (feminine -ሃ, written -ዋ after -ት/-ው) as object; ዐገትዋ is ዐገቱ + -ሃ, the object ለዐባይ ሀገር doubled by the suffix: ዐገተ 'besieged', ሮድዋ 'attacked' (?), ማህረከ 'plundered' (?), ፄወወ 'took captive'. በአፈ ኀጺን 'by the mouth of iron' = by the edge of the sword. Here Zion means Jerusalem, whose heart, the Ark, has just been removed. ፨ ends the unit.

sentences.t: ወደንገፀ ፡ ንጉሥኒ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ በእንተ ፡ ብካይ ፡ ወጽራኀ ፡ ሀገር ፡ ወሐወጸ ፡ እንተ ፡ ታዕካ ፡ ቤተ ፡ መንግሥት ፡ ቀልዐ ፡ ዘቤተ ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ወርእየ ፡ ኵላ ፡ ሀገር ፡ እንዘ ፡ ትበኪ ፡ ተትልዎሙ ፤
sentences.l: And-was-dismayed the-king too, Solomon, because-of the-weeping and-cry-of the-city, and-looked-out (?), which (እንተ) the-taʿka (?) of-the-house-of kingdom, the-citadel (?) of-the-house-of king, and-saw all the-city weeping, following-after-them;
sentences.i: King Solomon, too, was dismayed by the weeping and the outcry of the city, and he looked out (?) from the taʿka (?) of the royal house, the citadel (?) of the king's house, and saw the whole city weeping as it followed after them;
sentences.n: ደንገፀ 'was dismayed, startled'; -ኒ after ንጉሥ is 'too'. ብካይ 'weeping' and ጽራኀ 'cry' (construct before ሀገር). ሐወጸ 'he looked out / went to look' (?). እንተ is the feminine relative 'which', so 'from' is my guess at the sense (?). ታዕካ (taʿka) is left untranslated, as in ch. 25–26 and 43: apparently a part of the palace; ቀልዐ 'citadel' is a guess (?). ቤተ መንግሥት 'house-of kingdom' = the royal palace. እንዘ ትበኪ 'while she (the city) weeps'; ተትልዎሙ 'following them' (?).

sentences.t: ከመ ፡ ሕፃን ፡ ዘ ፡ አኅደገቶ ፡ ጥበ ፡ እሙ ፡ ወጐየት ፡ እምኔሁ ፡ ወይተሉ ፡ አሠረ ፡ እሙ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይጸርኅ ፡ ወይበኪ ፡ ከማሁ ፡ ኮኑ ፡ ይጸርኁ ፡ ወይበክዩ ፡ ወይወድዩ ፡ ሐመደ ፡ ዲበ ፡ ርእሶሙ ፡ ወያስሕዙ ፡ አንብዐ ፡ እምአዕይንቲሆሙ ።
sentences.l: Like a-child whom abandoned-him the-breast (?) of-his-mother and-she-fled from-him, and-he-follows after his-mother crying and-weeping — so they-were: crying-out and-weeping, and-putting ashes on their-heads and-letting-flow tears from their-eyes.
sentences.i: Like a child whom his mother has left (?), she having fled from him, and he follows after her crying and weeping — so they were, crying out and weeping, putting ashes on their heads and letting tears run from their eyes.
sentences.n: ከመ ሕፃን ዘ … ከማሁ ኮኑ 'like a child who … so they were'. The text has a spaced ዘ ('whom'). ጥበ እሙ — I take ጥበ as 'breast' (?), so 'his mother's breast abandoned him' (?), i.e. a child forsaken by his mother; I have smoothed this in the translation. ይተሉ አሠረ እሙ 'he follows his mother's track' (አሠር 'track, trace'). ይወድዩ ሐመደ ዲበ ርእሶሙ 'they put ashes on their heads', the standard mourning gesture. ያስሕዙ, with አንብዐ 'tears', must mean 'make flow', like ያውሕዙ earlier in the chapter; I take it as a variant spelling of that verb (?).

sentences.t: ወሰሎሞንሂ ፡ ተሀውከ ፡ ወርዕደ ፡ ሶበ ፡ ርእየ ፡ ግርማሆሙ ፡ ሰእለ ፡ ሖሩ ፡ ወተሀውከ ፡ አማዕዋቲሁ ፡ ወአንብዑ ፡ ታንጠበጥብ ፡ ዲበ ፡ ልብሱ ፤
sentences.l: And-Solomon too was-troubled and-trembled when he-saw their-majesty ሰእለ (?) they-went, and-were-stirred his-bowels and-his-tears dripped onto his-garment;
sentences.i: And Solomon, too, was troubled and trembled when he saw their majesty as they went (?); his inward parts were stirred, and his tears dropped onto his garment;
sentences.n: ተሀውከ 'was troubled, disturbed'; ርዕደ 'trembled'; ወሰሎሞንሂ — ሂ is an enclitic 'too, as for'. ሰእለ ሖሩ is unclear (?) — perhaps 'the sight of them as they went'. አማዕዋቲሁ 'his bowels, inward parts' (a plural, the seat of feeling; I do not know the singular (?)). ታንጠበጥብ 'it drips' (feminine because አንብዕ 'tears' takes a feminine singular verb).

sentences.t: ወይቤ ፡ ሴልየ ፡ እስመ ፡ ኀለፈት ፡ ክብርየ ፡ ወወድቀት ፡ አክሊለ ፡ ምክሕየ ፡ ወውዕየት ፡ ከርሥየ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ዘሖረ ፡ ዝንቱ ፡ ወልድየ ፡ ወነሠተ ፡ ግርማሃ ፡ ለህገርየ ፡ ወግዕዙ ፡ ደቂቀ ፡ ኀይልየ ፤
sentences.l: And-he-said, 'Alas (?), for has-passed my-glory, and-has-fallen the-crown-of my-boasting, and-has-burned my-belly because-of this who-went, this my-son, and-who-took-away (?) the-majesty-of-her of-my-city; and-have-departed the-sons-of my-strength;
sentences.i: And he said, 'Alas (?)! For my glory has passed away, and the crown of my boasting has fallen, and my belly burns, because of this my son who went and took away (?) the majesty of my city, and the sons of my strength have departed;
sentences.n: ሴልየ is unclear (?); I take it as an exclamation. ኀለፈት, ወድቀት and ውዕየት are fem. singular perfects ('has passed', 'has fallen', 'has burned'), agreeing with ክብር, አክሊል, ከርሥ. አክሊለ ምክሕየ 'crown-of my-boasting' is a construct chain. ከርሥ 'belly' as the seat of grief. በእንተ ዘሖረ 'because of him who went'. ነሠተ 'took away' (?). ህገርየ is Bezold's spelling (for ሀገርየ 'my city'). ግዕዙ 'they departed' (ግዕዘ). ደቂቀ ኀይልየ 'sons of my strength' = my mighty ones.

sentences.t: ወእምይእዜሰ ፡ ኀለፈት ፡ ክብርነ ፡ ወተሀይደት ፡ መንግሥትነ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሕዝብ ፡ ነቢር ፡ እለ ፡ ኢያአምርዎ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፤
sentences.l: And-from-now, indeed, has-passed our-glory and-has-been-carried-off our-kingdom to a-people dwelling (?), who not-know-him God;
sentences.i: And from now on our glory has passed away, and our kingdom has been taken away to a settled (?) people who do not know God;
sentences.n: ወእምይእዜሰ 'and from now on, indeed' (እም- 'from' + ይእዜ 'now' + emphatic -ሰ). ተሀይደት (fem. perfect) 'was carried off / given over' (?). ሕዝብ ነቢር — ነቢር 'dwelling, settled' (?); the sense 'foreign, living elsewhere' is a guess. እለ ኢያአምርዎ 'who do not know him' (እለ plural relative; ኢ- 'not').

sentences.t: በከመ ፡ ይቤ ፡ ነቢይ ፡ ሕዝብ ፡ እለ ፡ ኢኀሠሡኒ ፡ ረከቡኒ ፡ እምይእዜሰ ፡ ይትወሀቦሙ ፡ ሕግ ፡ ወጥበብ ፡ ወአእምሮ ፤
sentences.l: As said the-prophet, 'A-people who not-sought-me found-me'; from-now indeed will-be-given to-them law and-wisdom and-knowledge;
sentences.i: As the prophet said, 'A people who did not seek me have found me'; from now on law, wisdom and knowledge will be given to them;
sentences.n: Quotation of Isaiah 65:1 (cited again in Romans 10:20): a people who had not sought God are found by him. In ኢኀሠሡኒ and ረከቡኒ the final -ኒ is 'me' (the object suffix), not the enclitic 'too'. Then ይትወሀቦሙ ሕግ 'it will be given to them — law' (ተ-stem passive of ወሀበ 'give'; the thing given is the subject).

sentences.t: ወአቡየኒ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ በእንቲአሆሙ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይብል ፡ ይገንዩ ፡ ቅድሜሁ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ ወጸላእቱሂ ፡ ሐመደ ፡ ይቀምሑ ፤
sentences.l: And-my-father also prophesied about-them, saying, 'Will-bow before-him Ethiopia, and-his-enemies too dust will-taste';
sentences.i: And my father also prophesied about them, saying, 'Ethiopia will bow before him, and his enemies will taste dust';
sentences.n: Echoes Psalm 72:9 (71:9 in the Septuagint numbering) — 'Ethiopians' bow and enemies lick dust. ወአቡየኒ 'and my father too' (David, the psalmist, prophet). ይገንዩ 'they will bow' (ገነየ) and ይቀምሑ 'they will taste' (? the psalm has the enemies 'lick' the dust; I cannot confirm ቀምሐ either way) are imperfects with future sense; ጸላእቱሂ 'his enemies too'.

sentences.t: ወበካልእኒ ፡ ይብል ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ ትሜጥዎ ፡ እደዊሃ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወውእቱኒ ፡ ይትሜጠዋ ፡ በክብር ፡ ወነገሥተ ፡ ምድርኒ ፡ ይሴብሕዎ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፤
sentences.l: And-in-another he-says, 'Ethiopia will-hand-over-to-him her-hands, to-God, and-he-too will-receive-her with-honour; and-the-kings-of the-earth too will-praise God';
sentences.i: And in another place he says, 'Ethiopia will hand over her hands to God, and he will receive her with honour; and the kings of the earth will praise God';
sentences.n: Echoes Psalm 68:31–32 (67:32 in the Septuagint numbering). The Geʿez verb is ትሜጥዎ 'she will hand over to him' (መጠወ + -ዎ), with እደዊሃ 'her hands' as the thing handed over; the sense is the same gesture of submission, but 'stretch out' is not in this word. The ሜ of ትሜጥዎ is not the regular vowel of መጠወ, so ሜጠ 'turn' ('she will turn her hands to him') may be the verb instead (?). ይትሜጠዋ — 'he will receive her' (ተ-stem, ተመጠወ). ይሴብሕዎ 'they will praise him'. ወበካልእኒ 'and in another (psalm)'.

sentences.t: ወበሣልስኒ ፡ ይቤ ፡ ናሁ ፡ ኢሎፍሊ ፡ ወጢሮስ ፡ ወሕዝበ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ እለ ፡ ተወልዱ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ሕግ ፡ ይትወሀቦሙ ፡ ሕግ ፡ ወይብልዋ ፡ ለጽዮን ፡ እምነ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ብእሲ ፡ ዘተወልደ ፤
sentences.l: And-in-the-third too he-said, 'Behold the-foreigners (Philistines) and-Tyre and-the-people-of Ethiopia, who were-born without law: will-be-given to-them law, and-they-will-call Zion "our-mother" because-of the-man who was-born';
sentences.i: And in the third he said, 'Behold the foreigners, and Tyre, and the people of Ethiopia, who were born without the law: the law will be given to them, and they will call Zion "our mother" because of the man who was born';
sentences.n: Echoes Psalm 87:4–5 (86 in the Septuagint numbering). ኢሎፍሊ is the Greek word for 'foreigners' (Philistines), borrowed whole. ዘእንበለ ሕግ 'without law'. እምነ 'our mother' (እም 'mother' + ነ 'our'). ወበሣልስኒ 'and in the third': the third psalm cited. ናሁ 'behold'.

sentences.t: በእንተ ፡ ዝንቱኑ ፡ ወልድየ ፡ እንጋ ፡ ዘተወልደ ፡ እምኔየ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: Concerning this very son of mine, then (?), who was-born of-me?
sentences.i: Was it perhaps about this very son of mine, who was born of me? (?)
sentences.n: ዝንቱኑ — the enclitic -ኑ makes the sentence a question: 'about this very (son)?'. እንጋ is an emphasizing particle, 'then / indeed' (?). ዘተወልደ እምኔየ 'who was born from me'. Solomon wonders whether the prophecies he has just quoted refer to his own son, Menelik. ፨ ፨ close the chapter.
